responses.response: In this repo, the clean bootstrap is to create `projects/payments/` from `projects/template/`. The minimum files are: `projects/payments/likec4.config.json` (set the project `name` and `title`, keep `include.paths` pointing to `../shared`, keep `imageAliases.@` pointing to `../shared/images/`), `projects/payments/system-model.c4` (define payments actors, systems, containers, and relationships), and `projects/payments/system-views.c4` (add the index view and at least one C1/C2 view). `projects/payments/ADR/` is optional but useful for local architectural decisions. Practical sequence: copy the template, rename metadata, replace the sample `mySystem`/`user` model with payments elements, then add views. Use `projects/spec-showcase/` as a reference example, not as the source template.

Usually not in the current shared specifications area. In this workspace, `projects/shared/spec-*.c4` is clearly used for reusable specification assets such as element kinds, tags, relationship types, colors, and icons. Putting concrete business instances like `paymentsCore` and `backOfficeUser` into those spec files would mix conventions with domain content. Better rule: if they are mainly for the payments project, keep them in `projects/payments/system-model.c4`; if they are truly canonical across several projects, promote them into a separate shared model area such as `projects/shared/domain/` or `projects/shared/common-models/`, not into the spec files themselves. Cross-project references should use one canonical definition only: include the shared domain model from consuming projects, and avoid project-to-project include chains when possible. If another project needs a formerly local element, extract it once to shared instead of duplicating it.

Not by itself. `organize-multi-project` is the right skill for deciding project boundaries, folder layout, and what belongs in shared versus project-local files, but include paths and image aliases are configuration details. For that part, it should be combined with `configure-project-includes`. In this repo, both `projects/template/likec4.config.json` and `projects/spec-showcase/likec4.config.json` show the expected baseline: include `../shared` and map `@` to `../shared/images/`.

Do not dump everything into one shared bucket. The clean approach is to separate the concerns, but keep the structure shallow: keep `projects/shared/spec-*.c4` for technical conventions and reusable DSL/spec definitions, keep `projects/shared/images/` for common icons/assets, add a small `projects/shared/domain/` (or similarly named folder) for reusable business actors, systems, and relationships that genuinely belong to multiple projects, and keep `projects/<project>/` for project-specific models and views. That avoids a maze while still giving you a clear split between shared technical specs and shared business models. Good rule of thumb: if an element would still exist even if one project were deleted, it may belong in shared domain; if it mainly describes one bounded context, keep it local to that project.
